newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam's army marches on empty stomach.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam's army marches on empty stomach.

text.p: Vietnam's official army newspaper said on Thursday that soldiers needed more food and praised military units which had resorted to growing their own vegetables and raising their own livestock.

"With current meal standards and the price of food...it is very difficult to ensure an adequate meal which provides enough calories for soldiers," the Quan Doi Nhan Dan (People's Army) daily said in an editorial.
Urging self-help, the paper lauded the traditional resourcefulness of an army whose soldiers often had to live off a meagre diet of cassava and jungle grubs during the Vietnam War.

It said many units could spend an extra 500-800 dong (4.5-7.0 U.S. cents) on each meal by selling some of the food they produce themselves and noted that a high proportion of soldiers in such units had gained weight.

Communist Vietnam, one of the world's poorest countries, has made big cuts to its military since its forces withdrew from Cambodia in 1989. It is now estimated to have a force of around 572,000 personnel.
